subject: SOC2 materials + next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@cloudhaven.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T15:02:00Z
Subject: SOC2 materials + next steps

Hi Samir — great to meet today, and thanks for walking through CloudHaven's primary use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- We covered your latency and retention constraints for inference pipelines, and the team asked specifically for SOC 2 controls around data isolation and logging (you flagged retention logs as high priority).
- Attached: Redwood_SOC2_packet_v1.pdf (summary + attestation), redwood-security-factsheet.pdf.

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the SOC2 packet with your security team (happy to jump on a call to walk the packet).
2) If helpful, we can provide an anonymized sample of KV/cache logs and retention metadata — let me know what format you want.
3) Provide any specific evidence items your procurement/audit team needs and we'll route them to SRE/security.

Would you say your timeline for completing the security review is this month, or should we expect things to slip into June? I can book a 30-min sync with Rishi (copied) and our security SME.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_packet_v1.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-security-factsheet.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
On some threads I include the quick reference: we support private VPC deployments, dedicated GPU pools, and audit log exports for compliance reviews.

From: Samir Patel <samir@cloudhaven.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC2 materials + next steps

Hi Olga — thanks for the packet and the recap. I shared the PDFs with our security team and procurement. A couple quick notes from security: 

- They want a small sample of retention/log metadata (to validate KV cache eviction and retention timestamps).
- We may also need a short write-up on how key material is handled across Hosted vs Private deployments.

At the moment, security is still consolidating feedback; procurement has a few internal budget items to iron out so timeline might slip. I'm looping in CloudHaven Security (security@cloudhaven.ai) for any direct follow-ups.

If you can provide a CSV sample of anonymized KV traces and a one-page note on key management options across deployment modes, that would help speed things up. I'll aim to get consolidated feedback by next week but can't promise — two other audits just landed on our side.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudHaven
samir@cloudhaven.ai

Hi Samir — just checking in on the SOC2 review status and whether anything we provided is blocking your team. Per your note, we prepared an anonymized sample of KV/cache logs that mirrors the retention fields security asked about. I've attached a small CSV and a one-pager on key management options. Subject: Re: Checking in on SOC2 review — any blockers?

Hi Olga and Rishi — apologies for the slow reply. We are still gathering feedback; two higher-priority audits landed last week and pulled our security team's bandwidth. A few quick updates: 

- Security confirms the CSV sample looks like the right fields; they'll want a short walkthrough to validate assumptions around cache TTL/eviction behavior.
- Procurement flagged budget timing concerns; they indicated this will likely be moved into the Q3 procurement window unless we can get an executive sign-off for a June start.

Can we set a 20-minute call next week (Jun 1–4 window) for security walkthrough + a brief procurement alignment? I'm adding Maya (copied) from procurement to coordinate times. If you have a short deck or an exec one-pager that summarizes deployment options and SLAs, please drop it into the HubSpot deal (link below) and I'll make sure procurement sees it.

Thanks — I'll follow up after our security stand-up on Friday with confirmed times.

Best,
Samir
